source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 2 (i)-(ii): projections (book p.274). Key (PDF 311-312) prints vector projections; 14.2.3 defines the scalar; both given, correction callout.

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Calculate the projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) and projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\) when: \(\underline{a} = 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\)
blocks.explanation:
Two projections are asked: of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) and of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\).
By 14.2.3 the projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) is the number \(\frac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|}\) (divide by the length of the vector after 'along').
Plan: one dot product, two lengths, two divisions; then the vector forms, which the answer key prints.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\).
To find: the projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) and of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\).
Method: Projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) \(= |\underline{a}|\cos\theta = \dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|}\); projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\) \(= \dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{a}|}\). Multiplying the number by the unit vector of that line gives the vector projection.

Find the dot product
\[\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b} = (2)(1) + (3)(-2) + (-1)(4)\]
\[= 2 - 6 - 4 = -8\]
Why: Both projections use the same \(\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}\), so we find it once. The dot product is negative, so the angle is obtuse and both projections will be negative (the shadow points backwards).

Find the two lengths
\[|\underline{a}| = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 1} = \sqrt{14}\]
\[|\underline{b}| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 16} = \sqrt{21}\]
Why: \(|x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\).

Projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\)
\[\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|} = \dfrac{-8}{\sqrt{21}}\]
\[\text{Vector: } \dfrac{-8}{21}(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 4\underline{k})\]
\[= -\dfrac{8}{21}\underline{i} + \dfrac{16}{21}\underline{j} - \dfrac{32}{21}\underline{k}\]
Why: Divide by \(|\underline{b}|\), the length of the vector we project onto. Times \(\dfrac{\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|}\) gives the vector form \(\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|^2}\underline{b}\).

Projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\)
\[\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{a}|} = \dfrac{-8}{\sqrt{14}}\]
\[\text{Vector: } \dfrac{-8}{14}(2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k})\]
\[= -\dfrac{8}{7}\underline{i} - \dfrac{12}{7}\underline{j} + \dfrac{4}{7}\underline{k}\]
Why: Same dot product, but now divide by \(|\underline{a}|\); the vector form is \(\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{a}|^2}\underline{a}\).

Check
\[\tfrac{8}{21}|\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}|\]
\[= \tfrac{8\sqrt{21}}{21} = \tfrac{8}{\sqrt{21}}\]
\[\tfrac{8}{14}|2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}|\]
\[= \tfrac{8\sqrt{14}}{14} = \tfrac{8}{\sqrt{14}}\]
Why: The length of each vector projection equals the size of the number we found, so the two forms agree.
blocks.final_answer: Projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) \(= \frac{-8}{\sqrt{21}}\) (vector form \(-\frac{8}{21}\underline{i} + \frac{16}{21}\underline{j} - \frac{32}{21}\underline{k}\)); projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\) \(= \frac{-8}{\sqrt{14}}\) (vector form \(-\frac{8}{7}\underline{i} - \frac{12}{7}\underline{j} + \frac{4}{7}\underline{k}\))

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Calculate the projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) and projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\) when: \(\underline{a} = 4\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\)
blocks.explanation:
Two projections are asked: of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) and of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\).
By 14.2.3 the projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) is the number \(\frac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|}\) (divide by the length of the vector after 'along').
Plan: one dot product, two lengths, two divisions; then the vector forms, which the answer key prints.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = 4\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
To find: the projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) and of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\).
Method: Projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) \(= |\underline{a}|\cos\theta = \dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|}\); projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\) \(= \dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{a}|}\). Multiplying the number by the unit vector of that line gives the vector projection.

Find the dot product
\[\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b} = (4)(1) + (-2)(1) + (3)(1)\]
\[= 4 - 2 + 3 = 5\]
Why: Both projections use the same \(\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}\), so we find it once. It is positive, so the angle is acute and both projections are positive.

Find the two lengths
\[|\underline{a}| = \sqrt{16 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{29}\]
\[|\underline{b}| = \sqrt{1 + 1 + 1} = \sqrt{3}\]
Why: \(|x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\).

Projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\)
\[\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\]
\[\text{Vector: } \dfrac{5}{3}(\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k})\]
\[= \dfrac{5}{3}\underline{i} + \dfrac{5}{3}\underline{j} + \dfrac{5}{3}\underline{k}\]
Why: Divide by \(|\underline{b}|\), the length of the vector we project onto. Times \(\dfrac{\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|}\) gives the vector form \(\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|^2}\underline{b}\).

Projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\)
\[\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{a}|} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{29}}\]
\[\text{Vector: } \dfrac{5}{29}(4\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k})\]
\[= \dfrac{20}{29}\underline{i} - \dfrac{10}{29}\underline{j} + \dfrac{15}{29}\underline{k}\]
Why: Same dot product, but now divide by \(|\underline{a}|\); the vector form is \(\dfrac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{a}|^2}\underline{a}\).

Check
\[\tfrac{5}{3}|\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}|\]
\[= \tfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{3} = \tfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\]
\[\tfrac{5}{29}|4\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}|\]
\[= \tfrac{5\sqrt{29}}{29} = \tfrac{5}{\sqrt{29}}\]
Why: The length of each vector projection equals the size of the number we found, so the two forms agree.
blocks.final_answer: Projection of \(\underline{a}\) along \(\underline{b}\) \(= \frac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\) (vector form \(\frac{5}{3}\underline{i} + \frac{5}{3}\underline{j} + \frac{5}{3}\underline{k}\)); projection of \(\underline{b}\) along \(\underline{a}\) \(= \frac{5}{\sqrt{29}}\) (vector form \(\frac{20}{29}\underline{i} - \frac{10}{29}\underline{j} + \frac{15}{29}\underline{k}\))

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (PDF 311-312) prints only vectors, e.g. \(-\frac{8}{21}\underline{i} + \frac{16}{21}\underline{j} - \frac{32}{21}\underline{k}\). These are the vector projections. Section 14.2.3 defines the projection as the number \(\frac{\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b}}{|\underline{b}|}\), which is \(\frac{-8}{\sqrt{21}}\), \(\frac{-8}{\sqrt{14}}\) in (i) and \(\frac{5}{\sqrt{3}}\), \(\frac{5}{\sqrt{29}}\) in (ii). Both forms are given above; in an exam write the number and, if asked for a vector, the vector form.
